fields.title: Use client transactions only inside a batch
fields.decision: ArgentSea opens an ADO.NET client transaction in exactly one place: when executing a batch. All steps of a database or shard batch run on one connection in one transaction, committed after the last step and rolled back if any step throws. A shard-set batch runs as an independent transaction on each targeted shard. There is no cross-shard (distributed) transaction. Every other data method is a single command with no client transaction; any transaction it needs is managed server-side, inside the procedure or statement.
fields.context: Client-managed transactions hold locks across network round trips and are far less efficient than transactions inside a single procedure. The legitimate need for one is combining non-query operations, such as SQL Server bulk copy or a PostgreSQL COPY load, with queries atomically, or assembling a dynamic sequence of commands.

alternatives.option: Expose general client transactions (`BeginTransaction`) on every connection.
alternatives.whyRejected: It encourages chatty, lock-holding transaction patterns that the static-SQL design avoids.
Coordinator cost and availability coupling are at odds with independently failing shards.

fields.consequences: Most work runs as one round trip per call. Bulk loads can be committed together with the SQL that consumes them. A shard-set batch can partially succeed: some shards commit and others fail, so callers must make such work idempotent or compensate. Batches cost a round trip per step and should not replace a single multi-statement command.

sources.label: BatchAllAsync runs the batch independently on each targeted shard
